how_to_apply: Every recipe is a STARTING POINT in Anagram blocks. Apply the chain in the given order with add_block (Split before Merge, row 2 after both), then set_parameter for each setting, 2-4 at a time, asking the player to play between steps. Where a cabinet is listed, ask first whether the pedal feeds a PA/interface (keep it) or a real bass amp (skip or disable it). Gear named in 'idea' is a description of the sound, not a claim about what the artist used.

recipes.name: Classic rock
recipes.idea: Fingers or pick into a lightly pushed tube head: compressor for consistency, a warm overdrive at low blend for hair, an Ampeg/Marshall-style head carrying the mids, a cut below 100 Hz to tighten, a 4x10/8x10 cabinet.
recipes.confidence: Chain and values based on the Darkglass factory preset 'Vintage Microtubes' with the drive turned down; tune by ear.

chain.note: Even fingerstyle without killing the attack.
Hair, not distortion; raise Drive toward 7-8 for a dirtier rock tone.
Marshall-style mids; Volume up for breakup.
Tighten below 100 Hz, a little definition at 3 kHz.
Pick an Ampeg-style (Peggy) 8x10 or 4x10 with a Dynamic 421 mic via choose_cabinet.

ask: Does the pedal feed a PA/interface (keep the cabinet) or a real bass amp (disable it)?
Fingers or pick? Pick players usually want Treble 7 and the low shelf cut deeper.
How much dirt: hair, crunch or distortion?
scenes: Scene 2: VMT Drive 7, Blend 60 for the chorus.
Scene 3: VMT off for clean verses.
notes: If the low end gets loose, lower VMT Blend before touching the EQ.

recipes.name: Modern metal / djent
recipes.idea: Two voices in parallel: a clean, compressed, full low end on one row and a tight high-band grind on the other, gated, with the top fizz shelved off. Clear pick attack, no mud, works with low tunings.
recipes.confidence: Chain and values taken from the Darkglass factory preset 'Djentlemen' (crossover off, dirty row 1, clean row 2 with the cabinet). Strong starting point for this style.

chain.note: Both rows get the full range; row 1 is the dirty voice, row 2 the clean one.
Warm, barely driven clean voice.
The clean row owns the lows: boost the shelf, cut the top.
Cabinet on the clean row only; the dirty row stays direct.

ask: Tuning and number of strings? For B standard or lower, raise microtubes-x low_pass and the Split stays full range.
Pick or fingers? Pick players may want B3K MidBoost on.
Does the pedal feed a PA/interface or a real amp?
scenes: Scene 2: B3K off for a cleaner verse.
Scene 3: Merge Blend 70 for more clean voice under solos.
notes: Entropia alone (mid 'B3K Midboost', high 'Alpha Bite', clean compressed lows) gives a similar result in one block when slots are tight.
Fizz: lower DarkglassGEQ HighShelf on row 1 first, then B3K Tone.

recipes.name: Punk / DI rock
recipes.idea: Pick, fast and bright: a SansAmp-style DI preamp with moderate drive and presence, mids pushed so it cuts next to loud guitars, a compressor that lets the pick through, a 4x10 cabinet or none.
recipes.confidence: Chain from common DI-rock practice (SansAmp-style block + compressor); values are catalog defaults adjusted by the block guide. Tune by ear.

chain.note: Slow attack keeps the pick click.
Mids up: the SansAmp scoop disappears in a band.
A 4x10 with a Dynamic 421 (forward mids).

ask: PA/interface or a real amp?
How dirty: crunchy or full distortion (drive 8 with blend 90)?
notes: Presence (pres) is the fizz control: lower it before treble if it gets harsh.

recipes.name: Funk / slap
recipes.idea: Hi-fi and scooped: a slow-attack compressor so the thumb and pop transients pass, an SWR/EBS-style head with the aural-enhancer smile curve, a mild 500 Hz cut and a high shelf for sparkle, a bright condenser mic on the cabinet.
recipes.confidence: Chain from common slap practice; compressor attack/ratio are standard slap values, amp values are catalog defaults. The Darkglass Ignissor template 'Slap 'n' Pop' is an alternative for the compressor.

chain.note: 25 ms attack: the slap transient gets through, the sustain is evened.
SWR-style hi-fi; aurashaper is the one-knob smile curve.
SWR-style (SWIRL) 4x10 with a Condenser 103 for the top end.

ask: Active or passive bass? Active basses are already bright: lower treble and HighShelf.
PA/interface or a real amp?
Is the scoop too much in the band? Then raise mid to 5 and S500Hz to 0.
scenes: Scene 2: Gravitron (envelope filter, Mode BP) added at column 5 and enabled only here for funk lines.
notes: For an Ignissor instead of CompLim: fast attack and lower threshold on the high band catches pops while the lows stay free.

recipes.name: Jazz / clean fingerstyle
recipes.idea: Warm, even and quiet: a gentle optical-style compressor, a clean studio DI preamp for polish, a touch of low mids at 400-800 Hz for the note to speak, a dark microphone on a 1x15 or 2x10 cabinet, no drive.
recipes.confidence: Chain from common clean-bass practice with catalog defaults; a conservative starting point.

chain.note: Slow, smooth compression you feel rather than hear.
A 1x15 with a Condenser 67 (vintage, rolled-off top).

ask: Fretted or fretless? Fretless likes S800Hz +3 and a touch of chorus.
PA/interface or a real amp?
notes: Add Mint Chocolate Chorus (Blend 20, HPF Mid) after the EQ for the 80s fretless sound.

recipes.name: Motown / soul
recipes.idea: Round, dark and fat like a P-bass with flatwounds into a B-15 flip-top: tube combo breakup, no highs above 3 kHz, gentle compression, a 1x15 cabinet with a warm mic.
recipes.confidence: Chain from the classic recording setup as described by players; values are catalog defaults adjusted by the block guide. Tune by ear.

chain.note: Ampeg B-15-style; vol up for a little tube compression.
Flatwound darkness.
Peggy Fliptop 1x15 with a Condenser 67 or Dynamic 7.

ask: Roundwound or flatwound strings? With rounds, lower the LPF to 2500 Hz.
PA/interface or a real amp?
notes: Palm muting and foam at the bridge do more for this sound than any block.

recipes.name: Reggae / dub
recipes.idea: Deep, dark and dominant: bass and low mids forward, everything above 500-800 Hz rolled off, steady compression so every note weighs the same, a big 8x10 or 1x15 cabinet; dub adds a spring reverb or delay in a scene.
recipes.confidence: Chain from common reggae practice; the LPF value follows the Darkglass factory preset 'Boogie Boogie Honey' (533 Hz). Tune by ear.

chain.note: Lower toward 400 Hz for pure dub.
Peggy 8x10 or 1x15 with a Dynamic 112 (deep lows).

ask: Reggae (keep some 500-800 Hz) or dub (roll off lower)?
PA/interface or a real amp?
scenes: Scene 2: Spring Reverb (wet 3, lenght/length 6) or Analog Delay (Blend 30, Feedback 5) for dub drops.
notes: A high-pass at 35 Hz before the compressor keeps the sub clean on loud PAs.

recipes.name: Synth bass
recipes.idea: A real monophonic synth that follows the note: saw oscillators with an octave-up second oscillator, a resonant filter opened by the envelope, blended with the real bass, then a gate and a touch of chorus. Not a fuzz pretending to be a synth.
recipes.confidence: Chain built around the Axioma Mono Synth (Darkglass) with its catalog defaults adjusted; the factory 'Velcro Synth' preset is the fuzz/octave alternative. Tune by ear.

chain.note: First in the chain, single notes. Set instrument to the player's bass.
Keeps the synth level even.

ask: 4, 5 or 6 strings? (instrument option)
Synth only or synth under the bass? blend 10 = synth only, 5-7 = both.
Does the song want the arpeggiator (arp_enable, TempoBPM)?
scenes: Scene 2: cutoff 7, reso 7 for a brighter lead sound.
Scene 3: Axioma off for the real bass.
notes: For a dirtier 'fuzz synth' use the factory recipe: Subcitri + Chinchilla (Distortion 10, Tone 1.5, Blend 20) + Gravitron.
The app has an Axioma panel that draws oscillators, filter and envelope live.

recipes.name: Fuzz wall (two-piece band)
recipes.idea: Clean, compressed lows on row 1 and a fuzz-and-guitar-cab voice on row 2 above a crossover, so the riff sounds like bass and guitar at once; a gate after the fuzz, an octave-up option for the guitar illusion.
recipes.confidence: Chain follows the Darkglass factory presets 'Regal Blood' and 'DOOM' (parallel fuzz with a guitar cabinet); values from those presets and the block guide. Tune by ear.

chain.note: Lows stay on row 1, highs go to the fuzz on row 2.
A 4x12 with a Dynamic 57 for the guitar illusion.

ask: PA/interface or a real amp (then disable both cabinets)?
Should the fuzz voice sit an octave up? Add a Pitch Shifter (Semitone 12, DryLevel 10, WetLevel 6) at row 2 column 1 before the fuzz.
How much fuzz vs clean? Adjust Merge Blend.
scenes: Scene 2: Duality Fuzz off for a clean/compressed verse.
notes: If the low end thins at the Merge, add a Gain block on row 2 with PolarityInversion on and compare.

recipes.name: Modern clean (pop / worship / session)
recipes.idea: Polished, even and present: bus compression for glue, a sub-clean high-pass, a hi-fi head with a touch of low mids, a tube DI colour, a 4x10 with a neutral condenser.
recipes.confidence: Chain from common session practice; compressor values follow the Darkglass factory presets that start with the BUS Compressor. Tune by ear.

chain.note: Black & Yellow or Darkglass Neo 4x10 with a Condenser 414.

ask: PA/interface or a real amp?
Active or passive bass?
In-ears or wedges? In-ears usually want the cabinet Blend at 100.

recipes.name: Ambient / solo bass
recipes.idea: A clean, compressed bass into a modulated delay with the lows filtered out of the repeats, a long hall or shimmer reverb with trails, optional octave-up shimmer; chords and swells rather than grooves.
recipes.confidence: Chain follows the Darkglass factory presets 'Angelic Choir' and 'Synthy Shimmer'; values from the block guide. Tune by ear.
ask: Song BPM? Then set the delay Subdivision to '1/4 dot' or '1/8' with TempoBPM.
Stereo outputs? Use the Stereo reverb and delay variants.
PA/interface or a real amp?
scenes: Scene 2: ShimmerReverb Wet 8, Decay 8 for swells.
Scene 3: delay and reverb off for the groove parts.

recipes.name: Steve Harris (Iron Maiden) - starting point
recipes.idea: Clean but very aggressive: hard fingerstyle with flatwound strings, almost no distortion, treble and upper mids pushed hard so every note clanks, lows controlled, a big 4x10/8x10 cabinet. The attack is the sound, so compression must be slow or light.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the well-known clanky, bright, mostly clean Maiden bass sound; the exact amps, cabinets and settings he uses are not claimed here. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Slow attack: the finger clank passes untouched.
Pushes the upper mids into the amp.
SVT-style head, Ultra Hi on for the click.
Clear the mud, lift 1.6 and 3.2 kHz for the clank.
Peggy 8x10 with a Condenser 103 (bright, detailed).

ask: Flatwound or roundwound strings? Rounds already clank: lower S3200Hz to 1.
PA/interface or a real amp?
Should it stay totally clean, or do you want a hair of grind (add VMT Drive 2, Blend 30 after the compressor)?
scenes: Scene 2: GenericGEQ S1600Hz 6 and HBO Boost 7 for the galloping parts.
notes: Most of this tone is in the right hand: hard attack near the bridge pickup. Say so to the player.

recipes.name: Geddy Lee (Rush) - starting point
recipes.idea: Growling clean-with-edge: a DI-style preamp drive in parallel with a clean path, strong 500-1000 Hz growl, bright top, controlled lows. Two voices (clean + driven) summed, not a single distortion.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the familiar growly, parallel clean/dirty character of his later tone without claiming his exact rig. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Full range to both rows: clean on row 1, driven on row 2.
The growl: 800 Hz up.
SansAmp-style driven voice; row 1 keeps the clean lows.

ask: PA/interface or a real amp?
How much of the driven voice? Merge Blend 40 = cleaner, 60 = growlier.
Pick or fingers?
scenes: Scene 2: Merge Blend 70 and comic drive 8 for the heavy sections.

recipes.name: Flea (Red Hot Chili Peppers) - starting point
recipes.idea: Punchy, dry and in-your-face: fast solid-state head voicing with mids kept (contour off), a compressor with slow attack for slap, little or no reverb, a 4x10 with a mid-forward dynamic mic. Funk rock rather than hi-fi slap.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes his punchy funk-rock character; the exact amps and settings are not claimed. Values from the block guide and the factory 'Grona-Kulor' preset (GK-style head).

chain.note: GK-style punch with the mids in.
A 4x10 with a Dynamic 421.

ask: Slap-heavy or fingerstyle funk? For slap raise HighShelf to 3.
PA/interface or a real amp?
Any dirt? Add B3K Drive 4, Blend 40 after the compressor for the rockier songs.
scenes: Scene 2: Gravitron (Mode BP, Sensitivity 6) enabled for envelope-filter funk.

recipes.name: Jaco Pastorius - starting point
recipes.idea: Singing fretless: bridge-pickup bite with strong 800 Hz-1.5 kHz mids ('mwah'), clean with a little natural compression, a chorus for the famous doubled sound, bright but not clanky.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the bright, mid-forward fretless character; the exact gear is not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: The mwah lives at 800-1600 Hz.
A 4x10 or 2x12 with a Condenser 414 (neutral).

ask: Is the bass fretless? On a fretted bass this is a bright jazz tone; lower S1600Hz to 1.
PA/interface or a real amp?
Chorus always on, or only in a scene?
scenes: Scene 2: Chorus off; Scene 3: Digital Delay (Range 0.1-1 s, Blend 25, Feedback 3) for solos.

recipes.name: James Jamerson (Motown) - starting point
recipes.idea: The Motown sound: a Precision with old flatwounds, played with one finger, into a tube flip-top combo and a console compressor; dark, round, every note the same weight, no highs.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Follows the widely described recording setup (P-bass, flatwounds, B-15-style amp, console compression) without claiming exact settings. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Smooth optical-style levelling.
Peggy Fliptop 1x15 with a Condenser 67.

ask: Flatwound strings? With rounds lower the LPF to 2200 Hz.
PA/interface or a real amp?
notes: Foam under the strings at the bridge gives the thump no block can.

recipes.name: Cliff Burton (Metallica) - starting point
recipes.idea: Lead bass with heavy fuzz-distortion and a wah, played like a guitar: big scooped fuzz, a mid push so it still cuts, a wah set as a fixed filter (or on the expression pedal), a pushed tube head.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the distorted, wah-driven lead-bass character; exact gear is not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Fixed filter colour; bind it to the expression pedal in the app if there is one.
Big Muff-style fuzz with clean under it.

ask: Is an expression pedal plugged in for the wah?
PA/interface or a real amp?
Lead sound (this) or his rhythm sound (fuzz off, gain 5)?
scenes: Scene 2: fuzz off for rhythm parts.
Scene 3: wah Position 7 and pirate blend 100 for the solo.

recipes.name: Justin Chancellor (Tool) - starting point
recipes.idea: Mid-forward pick grind with a clean foundation: two voices in parallel, a clean compressed low path and a driven path with chorus, strong 500-1000 Hz, controlled top. The chorus on the dirty voice is part of the signature.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the parallel clean/grind-with-chorus character; exact amps are not claimed. Values from the block guide and the factory 'Djentlemen' parallel layout.

chain.note: Clean Mesa-style foundation on row 1.
The grind voice; MidBoost for the honk.
Keep the dirty voice out of the sub; row 1 owns the lows.

ask: Pick? This recipe assumes a pick near the bridge.
PA/interface or a real amp?
More grind or more clean? Merge Blend 65 / 45.
scenes: Scene 2: B3K Drive 8 and Merge Blend 65 for the heavy riffs.
Scene 3: row 2 blocks off for the clean sections.

recipes.name: Marcus Miller - starting point
recipes.idea: Hi-fi slap from an active Jazz bass: deep, scooped mids, very bright top, compression that lets the thumb through and controls the pop, an SWR-style head with the aural enhancer, a bright condenser on a 4x10.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the hi-fi scooped slap character; his exact rig and settings are not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Pops caught on the high band, lows free, mids slightly scooped.
SWIRL 4x10 with a Condenser 103.

ask: Active bass with the preamp boosted? Then lower HighShelf to 2 and treble to 5.
PA/interface or a real amp?
notes: The Darkglass Ignissor template 'Slap 'n' Pop' (in the app) is an alternative to the compressor settings above.

recipes.name: Lemmy (Motörhead) - starting point
recipes.idea: A bass amp cranked into a Marshall-style head with the mids all the way up and bass and treble pulled down, playing chords with a pick: amp distortion rather than a pedal, huge mids, ragged top.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the famous mids-up, bass-and-treble-down overdriven Marshall-style character; exact amps and settings are not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Chords stay clear without the sub.
Marshall-style head pushed hard: Volume is the breakup.
Extra grind if the amp alone is not ragged enough; otherwise disable it.
A 4x12-style guitar cab is also fair game here (cabinet-guitar with a Dynamic 57).

ask: PA/interface or a real amp?
Pick and chords, or single notes? For single notes raise Bass to 4.
Amp distortion only (B3K off) or more?
scenes: Scene 2: B3K off, JimBass Volume 7 for the quieter songs.

recipes.name: Chris Squire (Yes) - starting point
recipes.idea: Bi-amped Rickenbacker: the lows clean and solid, the highs sent to a driven guitar-style amp, so it growls and clanks on top of a full bottom. A crossover Split is exactly this.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the well-known bi-amped clean-low / driven-high character; exact gear is not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Lows on row 1, highs to the driven row 2.
Clean Fender-style low path.
Driven, bright voice on the highs.
Guitar cab on the high band only.

ask: PA/interface or a real amp (then disable both cabinets)?
Pick? This assumes a pick.
How much top growl? Merge Blend 60 = more.
scenes: Scene 2: VMT Drive 8 for the solos.

recipes.name: Duff McKagan (Guns N' Roses) - starting point
recipes.idea: Clean, punchy solid-state rock bass with an always-on chorus: GK-style head with the contour giving a slight scoop, a touch of chorus for width, pick attack kept by a slow compressor.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the famous clean-with-chorus 80s rock character; exact gear is not claimed. Values from the block guide and the factory 'Grona-Kulor' preset (GK-style head + chorus).

chain.note: A 4x10 with a Dynamic 421.

ask: Pick? Yes for this sound.
PA/interface or a real amp?
Chorus always on or only on some songs (scene)?
scenes: Scene 2: Chorus off.

recipes.name: John Entwistle (The Who) - starting point
recipes.idea: Loud, trebly, lead-style clean bass with a lot of string noise and attack: a British clean head on the edge of breakup, treble and presence up, lows kept moderate, a bright condenser on the cabinet, light compression only.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the bright, aggressive 'lead bass' character; exact amps and settings are not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Barely there: the dynamics are the point.
Hiwatt-style head on the edge.
A 4x10 or 8x10 with a Condenser 103.

ask: Roundwound strings and a hard attack? Both are part of the sound.
PA/interface or a real amp?
A hair of amp breakup (gain 8) or clean (gain 4)?

recipes.name: Pino Palladino - starting point
recipes.idea: Two eras. Neo-soul (this chain): a Precision with flatwounds, deep, dark and compressed, no highs, played behind the beat. 80s fretless: the same clean path with a round analogue octave down (Sublime) and a chorus; add them from the notes.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the dark neo-soul character and the 80s fretless-with-octaver sound in general terms; exact gear and settings are not claimed. Values from the block guide and catalog defaults.

chain.note: Peggy Fliptop 1x15 with a Dynamic 7 (thick low mids).

ask: Neo-soul (this) or the 80s fretless sound? For the latter add Sublime Octaver (CleanLevel 5, OctaveLevel 6, FilterCutoff 3) at column 1 after moving the compressor, and a Chorus (Blend 25).
Flatwound strings?
PA/interface or a real amp?

recipes.name: Les Claypool (Primus) - starting point
recipes.idea: Percussive slap, strum and tap with a vocal envelope filter, a fast compressor to even the technique, an SVT-style head with mids, and a bright top so every pop and tap reads.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. Describes the percussive, envelope-filter-heavy character; exact gear is not claimed. Values from the block guide and the factory 'Velcro Synth' Gravitron settings adapted to BP mode.

chain.note: Before the compressor so it reads the dynamics.

PA/interface or a real amp?

recipes.name: Adam 'Nolly' Getgood (Periphery) - starting point
recipes.idea: Produced modern metal bass: clean compressed lows, Darkglass-style multiband grind on mids and highs, gated, with an engineer's cabinet capture doing the final shaping. He is a Darkglass artist, so the Entropia and the Artists Cabinet (which includes his captures) are the natural blocks.
recipes.confidence: Starting point. The Artists Cabinet block ships Nolly captures (community/Darkglass naming); the drive settings are catalog defaults adjusted by the block guide, not his settings.

chain.note: Clean compressed lows, B3K mids, Alpha bite on top, fizz shelved at 6 kHz.
Pick a Nolly capture ('Blend', 'AllTheMids', 'ScoopyDoo'...) via choose_cabinet.

ask: Tuning? For drop tunings lower lo_lp_freq and mid_hp_freq to 150.
PA/interface or a real amp?
Which Nolly capture name shows in choose_cabinet's list? Pick 'Blend' first.
